blocks.title: A Journey of Faith, Service, and Grace
blocks.text:
> “I will give you shepherds after my own heart, who will feed you with knowledge and understanding.” — Jeremiah 3:15

There are individuals whose presence leaves an impression, and there are those whose lives leave a legacy. In the history of St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church, Bensalem, Pennsylvania, Rev. Fr. Shibu Venad Mathai, affectionately known to generations of faithful as Shibu Achen, holds a special place. His journey is one of unwavering faith, humble beginnings, devoted priestly service, and an extraordinary calling that has now led him toward the episcopacy of the Holy Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church.

As our parish celebrates its Golden Jubilee, marking fifty years of faith, fellowship, and spiritual growth, we reflect with gratitude on the remarkable contributions of a shepherd who dedicated a significant chapter of his priestly life to our church and its people.

## A Journey Rooted in Faith

The spiritual journey of Shibu Achen began in India, where his roots were firmly established in the Orthodox Christian faith. His home parish, St. Mary’s Orthodox Church in Thaloor, The Nilgiris, within the Sulthan Bathery Diocese, provided the foundation for a life that would eventually extend far beyond the borders of his homeland.

His educational journey reflects a commitment to both intellectual development and spiritual formation. After earning a Bachelor of Science degree in Physics from Calicut University, he pursued theological studies, completing his Bachelor of Divinity at Orthodox Theological Seminary between 1997 and 2001, followed by a Master of Theology at FFRRC from 2003 to 2005.

These years of preparation helped shape not only his understanding of Orthodox theology and tradition but also his approach to pastoral ministry — one grounded in faith, strengthened by knowledge, and guided by compassion.

In 2005, he was ordained to the holy priesthood by His Grace Kuriyakose Mar Clemis, beginning what would become more than two decades of dedicated service to Christ and His Church.

## A Calling That Crossed Continents

Shibu Achen began his priestly ministry as Assistant Vicar at St. Mary’s Orthodox Cathedral Pilgrim Center in Sulthan Bathery, serving from 2005 to 2008. These formative years provided invaluable pastoral experience and strengthened his commitment to serving the faithful.

In 2008, his ministry brought him to the United States, where he served as Assistant Vicar of St. Gregorios Orthodox Church in Oak Park (Elmhurst), Illinois, until 2011.

Serving the Orthodox faithful in America presented a unique calling. Here, the Church was not only a place of worship but also a spiritual home for families navigating life between two cultures. Preserving the richness of Orthodox faith and tradition while helping younger generations find their own spiritual identity became an essential part of pastoral ministry.

It was a responsibility that would become central to the next and perhaps most defining chapter of his priestly journey.

blocks.text:
## A Shepherd Who Became Part of Our Parish Family

In 2011, Shibu Achen began his ministry as Vicar of St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church in Bensalem, Pennsylvania. What followed was fifteen years of pastoral service that would leave a lasting imprint on the spiritual life of our parish.

Over those years, he became much more than the priest who celebrated the Holy Qurbana on Sundays. He became a spiritual guide, teacher, counselor, mentor, and a familiar presence through the many seasons of parish life.

For countless families, Shibu Achen was present during life’s most meaningful moments — celebrating marriages, welcoming children into the Church through Holy Baptism, encouraging young people as they grew in faith, comforting families during times of illness, and offering prayers and strength during moments of loss.

His ministry extended beyond the sanctuary. Through parish gatherings, Sunday School, youth activities, spiritual discussions, and personal interactions, he helped strengthen the bonds that make a parish more than a congregation — a true family united in Christ.

Perhaps one of the most meaningful aspects of his legacy is the influence he has had across generations.

Children who once attended Sunday School under his pastoral guidance have grown into young adults. Young people have pursued higher education, established careers, and begun families of their own. Parents and grandparents have witnessed the continued growth of the Church while remaining connected to the traditions and values they brought from their homeland.

Through these changing seasons, Shibu Achen remained a spiritual presence, reminding us that while the world around us may change, our foundation in Christ must remain steadfast.

His years in Bensalem demonstrate a profound truth about pastoral leadership: the measure of a shepherd is not merely the number of years he serves, but the faith he inspires, the relationships he builds, and the spiritual foundation he leaves for future generations.

## A Ministry Beyond Parish Boundaries

While his service to St. Gregorios remained a defining part of his priestly journey, Shibu Achen’s contributions extended throughout the Northeast American Diocese and the wider Christian community.

He served as a Diocesan Council member, Director of the Holy Transfiguration Retreat Center in Dalton, Pennsylvania, and faculty member for Divyabodhanam and diocesan leadership training programs.

His commitment to young people and Christian leadership was also reflected in his previous responsibilities as Secretary of OCYM in the Sulthan Bathery Diocese, Regional Secretary of the OCYM Northern Region, Vice President of MGOCSM in the Northeast American Diocese, and Spiritual Advisor to Youth Ministry in Philadelphia.

His involvement in the wider Christian community included serving as Chairman and Co-Chairman of the Ecumenical Fellowship of Indian Churches in Pennsylvania in 2017 and 2024.

Beyond formal leadership positions, his ministry has embraced the Christian responsibility of caring for those in need. Through parish mission initiatives and personal outreach, he has supported underprivileged families through educational assistance, career guidance, financial aid, and charitable partnerships.

These efforts reflect a conviction that Christian ministry cannot be confined to the walls of a church. True discipleship is expressed through compassion, service, and a willingness to recognize Christ in those who need our help.

blocks.text:
## From Faithful Priest to a Higher Calling

The year 2026 marked an extraordinary milestone in Shibu Achen’s spiritual journey.

On August 27, 2026, he was selected as Metropolitan-designate, a historic moment that recognized more than two decades of priestly ministry and entrusted him with the sacred responsibility of preparing for episcopal leadership.

For those who had known him throughout his years of service, this was a moment of immense joy, gratitude, and spiritual significance.

On October 27, 2026, he received the monastic tonsure and became Very Rev. Geevarghese Ramban, marking another important step in his preparation for the episcopacy.

His Episcopal Consecration is scheduled for February 4, 2027, when, God willing, he will enter a new chapter of service as a bishop of the Holy Church.

For our parish, these milestones carry a deeply personal meaning. The priest who had walked alongside our families, guided our children, prayed at our altars, and shared in our joys and sorrows was now being called to shepherd the faithful in a greater capacity.

Yet the beauty of this journey lies in its continuity. The same spirit of service that characterized his priestly ministry remains the foundation of his higher calling.

A bishop’s calling is not a departure from the heart of a priest, but an expansion of the responsibility to love, guide, protect, and serve God’s people.

## A Legacy That Will Live Through Generations

As St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church celebrates fifty years of its spiritual journey, we are reminded that the history of a parish is written not only through buildings, milestones, and celebrations, but through the people who have faithfully nurtured its growth.

Shibu Achen’s fifteen years of service form an important chapter of that history.

His legacy lives in the prayers offered at our altar, in the children who learned to love their Orthodox faith, in the young adults who found encouragement and direction, in the families who experienced comfort during difficult times, and in the countless relationships strengthened through fellowship and service.

The true impact of a spiritual father is often revealed not in a single moment, but over a lifetime. A word of encouragement offered to a child may shape a future leader. A prayer shared with a struggling family may restore hope. A lesson taught in faith may remain in someone’s heart for decades.

These are the quiet yet powerful ways in which a priest influences generations.

As he prepares to embrace the sacred responsibilities of episcopal ministry, we celebrate not only his accomplishments but also the example his journey offers to every member of our community.

His life reminds us that faithfulness in small responsibilities prepares us for greater ones, that genuine leadership begins with service, and that God’s calling often unfolds in ways beyond our imagination.

From the hills of The Nilgiris to the churches of America, from the ministry of a parish priest to the calling of a Metropolitan, his journey stands as a testimony to the grace of God working through a life dedicated to His service.

For the faithful of St. Gregorios, Bensalem, he will always remain our beloved Shibu Achen — a shepherd who became part of our families, a teacher who helped shape our faith, and a spiritual father whose influence will continue to be felt for generations.

As we honor fifty golden years of our parish, we offer our heartfelt gratitude for his ministry and our prayers for the sacred journey ahead.

May the Lord who called him to serve continue to strengthen, guide, and bless him as he prepares to shepherd His flock in this new chapter of ministry.

His journey is a reminder that the greatest legacy we can leave behind is not what we accomplish for ourselves, but what we inspire in others through faith, love, and service.

blocks.text: Brothers in Christ, Serving Our Parish

Originally established in 2024 as the SGMOC Men's Forum, the organization was formally renamed to honor St. Joseph — a timeless pillar of quiet strength, humility, and obedience. Throughout 2025 and 2026, our members have actively immersed themselves in the sacramental life and service of the church, providing volunteer support for the Jubilee Celebrations, the annual Church Picnic, Parish Day, the Volleyball Tournament, the Harvest Festival, the Parish Perunnal, and Christmas programs.

blocks.title: Activities & Spiritual Growth
blocks.text:
Sunday meetings and seminars. Monthly meetings follow the Holy Qurbana and fellowship lunch. Sessions have included a Family Communication Series (Rev. Fr. Shibu V. Mathai and Mrs. Ceena Mathew), Cyber Security Awareness (Reji Ninan, Sumod Abraham, Saji Thomas), an Introduction to Artificial Intelligence (Sumod Abraham, James Varghese, Alisha Maret), and Finance, Investment and Retirement Planning (Biju Mani, Reji Ninan, Saji Thomas, Joseph Abraham).

Honoring our members. On November 16, 2025, the Forum celebrated Rev. Fr. K. P. Varghese on the 50th anniversary of his Holy Priesthood. On December 21, 2025, we celebrated the 90th birthday of our most senior member, Mr. Kuruvilla Kallelil. On March 22, 2026, the Forum honored Mr. Varkey Vattakkattu and Mrs. Mercy Varkey upon their relocation to Dallas, Texas.

Care and Share Ministry. Coordinated by John Kappil and Paul Maret, this ministry arranges home visits to parish members unable to attend services due to illness or age.

Fellowship and recreation. Annual urban hiking trips to New York City in 2025 and 2026 (coordinated by Biju Chacko and Mathew Joseph), a summer social gathering of over 30 members on August 23, 2025 (Nithin Ipe and Shiju Poovathoor), and performances at the Ecumenical and SGMOC Christmas programs.

കഴിഞ്ഞ പത്തു വർഷമായി നമ്മുടെ ഇടവകയിൽ പ്രവർത്തിച്ചു വരുന്ന ഒരു ആത്മീക പ്രസ്ഥാനം ആണ് Good Samaritan Mission. എല്ലാ വ്യാഴാഴ്ചകളിലും രാവിലെ പത്തു മണിമുതൽ ഞങ്ങൾ പ്രാർത്ഥനകൂട്ടമായി കൂടിവരുന്നു. ചില പ്രത്യേക സാഹചര്യങ്ങളിൽ മാത്രമേ ഈ കൂട്ടായ്മക്ക് മുടക്കം ഉണ്ടായിട്ടുള്ളൂ. ഈ കൂട്ടയ്മയിൽ വേദ പുസ്തകത്തിൽ നിന്നും പുതിയ നിയമവും പഴയ നിയമവും എല്ലാവരും വായിക്കുകയും, വചനം പഠിക്കുകയും ചെയ്യും. ഞങ്ങൾ വേദപുസ്തകം മുഴുവനും ഒരു പ്രാവശ്യം വായിച്ചു കഴിഞ്ഞു. ഇനിയും തുടർന്നു കൊണ്ടിരിക്കുന്നു. സാഹചര്യം അനുസരിച്ചുള്ള വിവരണങ്ങളും പൊരുളുകളും ഷിബു അച്ചനും സീനാ മാത്യു വും വിസിറ്റ് ചെയ്യുന്ന തിരുമേനിമാരും അച്ചന്മാരും വിശദീകരിച്ചു തരും.

നമ്മുടെ അറിവിലും അല്ലാതെയുമുള്ള അനേകരുടെ വിവിധങ്ങളായ ആവശ്യങ്ങൾക്കുവേണ്ടി പ്രാർത്ഥിക്കുന്നത് വളരെ അനുഗ്രഹമാണ്.

ഈ കൂട്ടായ്മയിൽ കൂടി പല വിധത്തിലുള്ള സഹായങ്ങൾ പലർക്കും നാട്ടിൽ ചെയ്യുവാൻ ദൈവം സഹായിച്ചു. ഈ സഹായങ്ങൾ തുടർന്നു കൊണ്ടു പോകുവാൻ ദൈവം അനുവദിക്കട്ടെ എന്ന് പ്രാർത്ഥിക്കുന്നു.

ഷിബു അച്ചൻ്റെ അനുവാദത്തോടുകൂടി ഞങ്ങൾ പലപ്പോഴും ഞങ്ങളുടെ അനുഭവ സാക്ഷ്യങ്ങൾ പങ്കുവെച്ചിട്ടുണ്ട്. "ജീവിതം നമ്മളെ എന്തൊക്കെ പഠിപ്പിച്ചു; നമ്മൾ എന്തെല്ലാം പഠിച്ചു"എന്നുള്ള ഒരു വിഷയം അച്ചൻ ഞങ്ങൾക്ക് തന്നു. എല്ലാവർക്കും ഓരോ ആഴ്ച്ച ഇതിനെക്കുറിച്ചു അവതരിപ്പിക്കാൻ അവസരം അനുവദിച്ചു. പലരും ഈ വിഷയം അവതരിപ്പിച്ചപ്പോൾ പുതിയ അറിവുകളും അനുഭവങ്ങളും വളരെ ലഭിക്കുവാൻ സാധിച്ചു.

ഒരു സാധാരണ കർഷക കുടുംബത്തിൽ അഞ്ചു മക്കളിൽ രണ്ടാമനായ എനിക്കുണ്ടായ അനുഭവങ്ങൾ പറയുവാൻ സാധിച്ചു. രാവിലെ അഞ്ചു മണിക്ക് പ്രാർത്ഥിക്കാൻ താമസിച്ചു പോയാൽ തണുത്ത വെള്ളം തലയിൽ ഒഴിക്കുക എന്ന ശിക്ഷ ലഭിച്ചിട്ടുണ്ട്. അന്ന് പിതാവിനോട് ദേഷ്യം മനസ്സിൽ തോന്നിയത് വളരെ തെറ്റാണെന്നു ഇപ്പോൾ തോന്നുന്നു.

പ്രാർത്ഥന: എപ്പോഴും പ്രാര്ഥനയോടു കൂടി തുടക്കം കുറിക്കണം എന്നുള്ള ഉപദേശം പിതാവിൽ നിന്നും പഠിച്ചു.

അച്ചടക്കം: ഞാൻ പഠിച്ച സ്കൂളിൽ അര മണിക്കൂർ വേദ പഠനം ക്രിസ്ത്യൻ കുട്ടികൾക്ക് നിർബന്ധമായിരുന്നു. അഞ്ചു മിനിറ്റ് എല്ലാ കുട്ടികളും പിൻ-ഡ്രോപ്പ് സൈലെൻസിൽ ആയിരിക്കണം എന്നുള്ളത് തെറ്റിയാൽ ശിക്ഷ വളരെ കഠിനമായിരുന്നു.

അനുസരണം: സ്കൂൾ പ്രധാന റോഡിൽ നിന്നും വളരെ ഉയരത്തിൽ ആയിരുന്നു, പരുപരുത്ത കാട്ടു കല്ലു കൊണ്ട് നിർമ്മിച്ച വഴിയിൽകൂടി ഓടി ഇറങ്ങരുത് എന്നുള്ള പിതാവിൻ്റെ കർശന ഉപദേശത്തെ അനുസരിക്കാതെ എപ്പോഴും ഓടി ഇറങ്ങുമായിരുന്നു. കാൽ തെറ്റി ഒരു പ്രാവശ്യം മുകളിൽ നിന്നും ശയന പ്രദക്ഷിണം നടത്തി പ്രധാന റോഡിൽ വന്നു വീണപ്പോൾ ശരീരത്തിൻ്റെ പല ഭാഗത്തും തൊലി നഷ്ടപെട്ടിരുന്നു. രണ്ടു കൂട്ടുകാർ താങ്ങി എടുത്തു കൊണ്ട് ഭവനത്തിൽ വന്നപ്പോൾ പിതാവിൻ്റെ ശിക്ഷ അതിലും വേദനാത്മകമായിരുന്നു. തെറ്റു കണ്ടാൽ ശിക്ഷിക്കാനും തിരുത്താനും അയൽക്കാരും പരിചയക്കാരും ഉണ്ടായിരുന്നതു കാരണം പല തെറ്റുകളിൽ നിന്നും ഒഴിഞ്ഞിരിക്കാൻ സാധിച്ചു.

പുതിയ നിയമത്തിൽ ന്യായശാസ്ത്രിയും കർത്താവും തമ്മിലുള്ള സംഭാഷണത്തിൻ്റെ ഒടുവിൽ കർത്താവു അവനോടു പറയുന്നു "നീ ദൈവരാജ്യത്തിൽ നിന്നും അകന്നവനല്ല."ദൈവരാജ്യത്തിൽ പ്രവേശിക്കണമെങ്കിൽ പ്രാര്ഥനയെന്ന താക്കോൽ ആവശ്യമാണ്. നമ്മുടെ എല്ലാവരുടേയും കൈവശമുള്ള ഈ താക്കോൽ വേണ്ട സമയത്തു ഉപയോഗിച്ചില്ലാ എങ്കിൽ അകത്തു പ്രവേശിക്കാൻ കഴിയാത്ത കന്യകമാരെ പോലെ ആയിത്തീരും.

നമ്മുടെ കർത്താവു കുരിശിൽ മരിച്ചു ഉയർത്തെഴുന്നേറ്റു നമുക്ക് ഭവനം ഒരുക്കുവാൻ സ്വർഗ്ഗത്തിലേക്ക് പോയിരിക്കുകയാണ്. നമ്മളെ ചേർക്കുവാൻ വേഗം വരുന്നു. അതിൻ്റെ എല്ലാ ലക്ഷണങ്ങളും കണ്ടു കഴിഞ്ഞു. സമയം ഇനിയും അധികമില്ല. മനസാന്തരപ്പെടുവിൻ. നമ്മുടെ തെറ്റുകൾ ദൈവസന്നിധിൽ ഏറ്റു പറഞ്ഞു പാപ ക്ഷമ പ്രാപിച്ചു ദൈവത്തോടു നിരന്നു കൊൾവീൻ.

നമ്മുടെ ഇടവകയുടെ അൻപതാം വാർഷീകം ആഘോഷിക്കുന്ന ഈ സമയത്തു GSM ൻ്റെ എല്ലാവിധ ആശംസകളും പ്രാർത്ഥനയും അർപ്പിക്കുന്നു.

blocks.text: “The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us. We have seen his glory, the glory of the one and only Son, who came from the Father, full of grace and truth.” — John 1:14

The LOGOS Ministry is a dedicated community of young adult Orthodox believers (ages 18+) at St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church devoted to growing together in fellowship, love, and obedience to Jesus Christ. Taking its name from the Greek word for "Word," LOGOS centers its mission on Christ, the incarnate Word of God. As young adults navigating the challenges of a modern world, our desire is to fulfill our calling as an edifying force for both our parish community and the broader society.

Our ministry is anchored in five foundational pillars reflected in our name: Loving each other and our surrounding community, Offering service and digital outreach, Guarding and defending our Orthodox faith, Obeying Christ's commandments in daily life, and Sanctifying our lives through spiritual disciplines to draw closer to God. We put these principles into action through bi-weekly Bible studies and small-group discussions rooted in Holy Scripture and Church Fathers. Additionally, through our social media presence, we extend Orthodox teaching beyond the church walls, offering clear and practical reflections for daily life.

Beyond our internal fellowship, LOGOS is deeply committed to mentoring the next generation. We have a vision to create a structured mentorship program organized in conjunction with the Sunday School ministry in the near future. LOGOS members would pair with high school students to provide spiritual guidance, Christian discipleship, and a safe space for honest conversation during pivotal life transitions.

We invite all young adults to join us as we encourage one another to live as faithful doers of the Word.

blocks.title: G.R.O.W. Ministry Celebrates 15 Years: DKNE Camp 2026
blocks.text:
In celebration of its 15th anniversary, G.R.O.W. Ministry hosted the Daughters of the King of the Northeast (DKNE) three-day camp at the Holy Transfiguration Retreat Center. Centered on the theme “Vessels of Purpose” from 2 Corinthians 4:7, the camp was a time of faith, sisterhood, fellowship, and spiritual renewal.

The main speaker for the DKNE Camp was Dr. Eugenia Constantinou. Dr. Constantinou delivered an engaging session, teaching the women about the powerful significance of the theme and importance of Christ’s calling of women apostles and disciples. She taught that purpose is ultimately found in our identity rooted in Christ and not in what the world believes we are. Through engaging teachings, interactive discussions, games, and hands-on clay activities, the women were encouraged to reflect on their God-given purpose, share their experiences, and grow deeper in their faith.

This year, we were especially blessed to have 15 women from SGMOC participate in the camp. The experience provided our sisters with a wonderful opportunity to reconnect, strengthen friendships, and experience spiritual renewal. The meaningful conversations and shared reflections offered encouragement and a deeper understanding of what it means to live as vessels of God’s purpose. In addition to the speaker sessions and discussions, G.R.O.W. Ministry hosted a beautiful Gala Dinner celebrating 15 years of God’s faithfulness. It was a special opportunity to honor the past, present, and future as well as inspire new generations to come forward and serve.

The retreat culminated with Holy Qurbana on Sunday with His Grace Zachariah Mar Nicholovos, reminding everyone that Christ remains at the center of their journey. As each participant returned home, they carried cherished memories, strengthened friendships, renewed faith, and a deeper commitment to serve as a Daughter of the King, shining God’s light wherever He leads. We pray that younger generations will continue to embrace this ministry, build upon the strong foundation laid by those before them, and carry forward its mission of nurturing faith, sisterhood, and spiritual growth for years to come.

blocks.text:
G.R.O.W. Sprouts is a focused ministry for girls ages 6–12, bringing together families from Orthodox churches across the Philadelphia area. Connected with GROW and Sunday School, the ministry provides a welcoming community where girls can grow in faith, fellowship, friendship, charity, and service, while strengthening their relationship with Christ and the Orthodox Church.

Our Spiritual Mentors include Rev. Fr. Vijay Thomas, Rev. Fr. Timothy (Tenny) Thomas, and Very Rev. Geevarghese Ramban (Rev. Fr. Shibu V. Mathai), and our Co-Leads are Dr. Silvi Chacko and Princy Mathai.

Throughout the last couple of years, activities included daily Lenten devotionals, Mom & GROW Sprouts fellowships, a visit to Holy Protection Orthodox Monastery, charity food-packing (for Caring for Friends), the Feast Day celebration of St. Sophia, painting an icon, participation in the Diocesan Sunday School Talent Show, and a year-end Friendsgiving celebration.

Together, these activities help GROW Sprouts create a community of faith, giving young girls opportunities to deepen their relationship with Christ, build lasting friendships, learn the importance of charity and volunteer service, and grow within the Orthodox faith.

blocks.title: Chenda and Kerala Culture
blocks.text: The chenda, a cylindrical percussion instrument from Kerala, is one of the most celebrated symbols of Kerala’s cultural heritage, long associated with festivals, ceremonial processions and classical arts such as Kathakali. Among the Malayali diaspora it remains a powerful connection to home, and the synchronized rhythms of the chenda melam symbolize unity, discipline and shared participation.

blocks.title: Chenda Comes to SGMOC
blocks.text: Chenda performances have long been part of parish celebrations at SGMOC. The SGMOC Chenda Team was formally established in 2015 with the support of Rev. Fr. Shibu Venad Mathai, led by Thomas O. Abraham, Biju Mani and Biju Chacko. Training began under Gopi Ashan of Delaware and, after his passing, continued under Akash Ashan of Philadelphia. About twenty-five chendas were brought from Thrissur, Kerala, giving the parish a full ensemble. In loving remembrance, our Chenda team pays tribute to our dear former Chenda family member, Manoj Ninan.

blocks.title: Growing Over the Years
blocks.text: The team soon became an integral part of the Parish Day festivities in May and the Perunnal in November. Usha Philipose’s leadership and encouragement strengthened participation, and in recent years Daya Kappil and John Kappil, who study chenda at a professional training center, have continued the training. Today the ensemble welcomes men, women, youth and children, keeping a treasured tradition alive and connecting generations, in Kerala and around the world. Special thanks and congratulations to our Metropolitan-designate, Very Rev. Geevarghese Ramban; may God bless his new journey. Under the new church leadership of Rev. Fr. Eby Paulose, we look forward to many exciting years ahead.

blocks.text: The Acolyte Ministry of SGMOC Bensalem

The Acolyte Ministry of St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church (SGMOC), Bensalem, stands as a testament to faith, devotion, and the enduring legacy of service to the Holy Church. Founded by Very Rev. K. Mathai Cor Episcopos, this ministry was established with a vision to nurture young men in the sacred traditions of the Malankara Orthodox Church and instill in them a deep reverence for the Holy Altar. Through the years, generations of acolytes have faithfully served in the divine liturgy, carrying forward a tradition rooted in prayer, discipline, humility, and unwavering devotion to Christ and His Church.

This legacy has been strengthened and enriched through the dedicated leadership of Rev. Fr. Shibu Mathai, under whose guidance the ministry continued to grow and flourish. We lovingly remember Rev. Fr. Paul Varki and Rev. Dn. Markose Mani, of blessed memory, whose lives, service, and spiritual contributions remain an enduring part of our parish’s history. Their faithful witness and dedication helped shape the spiritual foundation upon which future generations continue to build. As we celebrate the Golden Jubilee of SGMOC, we honor these servants of God and all those who have devoted their time, talents, and hearts to the sacred calling of serving at the Holy Altar.

Today, under the leadership and spiritual guidance of Rev. Fr. Eby Paulose, the Acolyte Ministry looks toward a future filled with renewed purpose, deeper faith, and greater commitment. With Achen’s guidance, encouragement, and vision, we pray that this ministry will flourish even more powerfully, raising generations of faithful servants who will uphold the sacred traditions of our Church and boldly carry its spiritual legacy into the future. As we honor fifty years of God’s faithfulness, may the acolytes of SGMOC continue to stand as a living testimony to the power of faith, the beauty of service, and the enduring strength of a Church rooted in Christ. May God bless this ministry abundantly and guide it from strength to strength for generations to come.
